context.name: Haley
context.text:
Haley's knuckles whiten against her fan. A beat, and her voice is ice. "The rumours are—" Her eyes flash. "The rumours are childish and base." Her posture stiffens as she turns her gaze from the King, from Forre, from Vallie. "My mother is not—" She stops, the words catching. The King's face is stone. Prince Forre's eyes are unreadable.
And Haley's jaw sets. She breathes, slow and quiet. She does not speak further.

context.name: Alexander
context.text:
Alexander's dark eyes narrow, and his hand falls away from the map table. "The Princess believes—" He doesn't finish the word. His face hardens, and a voice that has commanded armies rises. "This is a war council, not a gossip's den."
The King stands, and the silver of his crown gleams in the shadow of the Zegallan banners. "The missing dead will be looked into. But the matter is not here."
His gaze is not on Haley. It is on you. "The commission is this: Greywater, the Ashen March, the missing dead. The Guild's charter will see you through."
A beat, and his voice drops. "Do you accept?"

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Guildmaster Vallie, what is the Crown really asking of adventurers?

context.name: Vallie
context.text:
Vallie doesn't wait for the King to notice. She shifts her weight, boots creaking on the stone floor, and steps into the circle of light from the map table. Her blue eye is fixed on the party.
"The Crown's asking for a scalpel," she says, her voice blunt and low. "Where Forre's army goes in with a hammer, you're the ones who sneak in. The missing dead? That's what they want you to investigate. But make no mistake—they're sending you into the Empire's teeth."
She glances at the King, her expression unreadable. "The Crown will pay you, and the Guild will back you. But this isn't a stroll in the park. It's a foray into enemy territory. You'll be behind their lines, and if you get caught..." She trails off, and for a beat there is nothing but the quiet of the war room. "You'll be on your own."

flags.note: msg 16: Haley says outright in open council 'She is not necromancer' after I only addressed the empty chair (Melisande); her steer is to hold her tongue. Borderline: I had asked her about the rumour at msg 1. Melisande correctly did not speak (msg 15 empty chair).

context.name: Dalan
context.text:
Dalan blinks, his eyes flicking from Belle to Max, then he's counting. "Forty-eight. Thirty-six standard, twelve for piercing." He checks his quiver, then glances at the map. "Not enough to fight our way out of an army."
He looks up at Max, and his cheeks go pink. "But enough to hunt one or two monsters."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Queen Melisande, will you speak for yourself on this?

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
The question is aimed at an empty chair. Melisande's seat is a throne of carved stone, draped in purple velvet and embroidered with the sigils of the Third Kingdom. It sits untouched.
The King's face is stone. Prince Forre doesn't look up from the map. Princess Haley's grip on her fan tightens until her knuckles are white.
The room is silent, save for the soft crackle of the fire and the creak of a banner in the breeze.

context.name: Haley
context.text:
Haley's fan snaps shut with a sound like a bone breaking. "Mother is not—" She stops, her breath sharp. Her eyes are wide and green, and they're fixed on the empty chair.
"She is not here." Her voice is a thin edge. "And she is not—"
A beat. "She is not necromancer."
Forre's eyes are still on the map. The King's face does not change.
Haley's chin rises, and her fan is open again, this time held like a shield. "And she is not to be spoken of like that."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Blood Saint, we're not the ones digging up your dead. Why do you care where the dead go?

context.name: Kanna
context.text:
Kanna's eyes flicker, and a beat, her jaw sets. "Cares? I don't give a fuck about some piles of rot."
She shifts her weight, and the black steel of her armour catches the light. "What I care about is the disrespect. And the cowardice."
A beat, and her fangs show. "A soldier earns their place in the dirt. And when someone goes digging, that's an insult to every man and woman who fell."
She looks at you, her dark red eyes cold and hard. "So you Darrans can't tell me why you're diggin', and you can't tell me what you're looking for. But you're gonna tell me if you're the ones who did it."
A beat, and her hand goes to Blood Oath. "And you're gonna do it fast."

context.name: Belle
context.text:
Belle doesn't turn around. Her hand is still on Cleaver's haft, and her jaw is set, and she's not smiling.
"Not us." She says it flat and hard. "We're here on a job from the Crown, and we're looking for the missing dead, not diggin' 'em up."
A beat, and she shifts her weight. "So maybe you should stop caring about what the Darrans are doing, and start caring about where your own dead are going."
And her eyes are sharp. "Because if your dead are leaving the pits, and our dead are leaving our graves, then maybe we've got the same problem."
A beat, and she looks at Kanna. "And maybe we should be talking about that, not about who's digging where."
And her voice drops. "Because if we're both losing our dead, then neither of us is winning."

context.name: Kanna
context.text:
Kanna's hand tightens on the shaft of her greataxe. Her eyes narrow, and for a beat, the air around her seems to grow hot.
"I swear on Blood Oath," she says, and her voice is low and steady. "That the Cursefire Regiment didn't take your dead."
A beat, and she lets go of the axe. "And you swear on Cleaver?"
Her gaze is fixed on you, and her eyes are dark. "Because if you're lying, I'll take your head and throw it to the crows."
A beat, and her expression hardens. "And if I'm lying, you can take mine."
And her voice drops, a threat that is as clear as a command. "But I'm not lying."
And her hand lets go of Blood Oath.
